adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256,315-317 — `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is already falsy, so it searches for externalId===undefined which never matches — dead fallback, breaks per-host calendar targeting on update/delete. (P1, confidence 85)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback branch is:

`externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`

That `find(...)` executes only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null/""), so it effectively searches for `cal.externalId === undefined` (or null), which will almost always return no match and yield `undefined`. This makes the fallback logic dead/incorrect and prevents selecting a calendar from `destinationCalendar` when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided, potentially causing updates/deletes to target the wrong calendar (or fall back to default behavior elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — `booking.references.find(...)` (singular) was missed when converting the merge/reschedule stale-event cleanup path to multi-reference; only one arbitrary host's old calendar event gets deleted on reschedule/merge, leaving orphaned duplicates for other hosts. (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts the code was updated to treat calendar references as an array (e.g., `calendarReference = ...filter(...)` and iterating over them). However, in the merge/reschedule cleanup branch it still does `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`, which will select only a single calendar reference even if multiple `_calendar` references exist (now supported). That means the stale-event deletion path can delete only one old calendar event, leaving other hosts’/credentials’ old calendar events undeleted (orphaned duplicates). This is a concrete inconsistency visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:339-374 — `createAllCalendarEvents` does sequential unbatched `prisma.credential.findUnique` per host inside the loop instead of a batched `findMany`/parallel fetch (N+1); also destinations without `credentialId` sharing the same `integration` type can create duplicate calendar events. (P2, confidence 70/60)

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the new loop over `event.destinationCalendar` does an `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside the `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` path when the credential isn’t in `this.calendarCredentials`. This is a classic per-item DB fetch done sequentially (no batching/parallelization), which is verifiable from the diff.

Also, for destinations **without** `credentialId`, the code filters credentials by `c.type === destination.integration` and creates events for *all* matching credentials, but it does this inside the per-destination loop. If there are multiple destination entries with the same `integration` and no `credentialId`, the same set of credentials will be processed multiple times, producing duplicate calendar event creations. This duplication risk is directly implied by the shown control flow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce three similar Prisma fallbacks (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, EventManager.updateBookingReferences loop, and handleCancelBooking) using `prisma.credential.findUnique` when an in-memory credential isn’t found, so the “duplicated in 3 places” part is verifiable. However, the rest of the finding (“breaking constructor-scoped-credentials boundary” and “never revalidated against the `_calendar` type invariant”) is largely architectural/speculative rather than a concrete defect: the code fetches by `credentialId` coming from existing destination/reference data, and there’s no diff evidence that a non-calendar credentialId can appear here or that missing a type check causes an actual bug/regression. This is a maintainability/design critique, not a clearly verifiable correctness/security problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts updateEvent/deleteEvent — dead fallback logic (same as architecture #4) makes destination-calendar lookup inconsistent between create vs update/delete. (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the new fallback branch is effectively dead/incorrect:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the fallback runs), it searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it will not match any real calendar externalId and will return `undefined`. Same pattern is used for `calendarId` in deleteEvent. This makes update/delete unable to reliably derive a calendarId from `destinationCalendar`, and it is inconsistent with createEvent which now selects by `credentialId`.

So the finding describes a real, verifiable correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:344-366,517-539 and handleCancelBooking.ts:429-440 — unscoped `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })` extended to 3 new call sites with no ownership/host validation before using the credential to mutate an external calendar; weakens the trust boundary that previously limited calendar mutation to the organizer's own credential set. (P2, confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple new fallbacks that fetch a calendar credential directly from the DB by id (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, EventManager.updateCalendarEvents, and handleCancelBooking). In each case, if the credential is not found in the organizer/user’s in-memory credential set (this.calendarCredentials or bookingToDelete.user.credentials), the code now does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })` (or with only `include` for app slug) and then proceeds to call calendar mutation operations (createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent) using that fetched credential. There is no added check that the fetched credential belongs to the booking’s user/team or is otherwise authorized, so an arbitrary credentialId present in `destinationCalendar` or in booking `references` could be used to mutate an external calendar via someone else’s credential. This is a concrete trust-boundary weakening introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256,315-317 — self-referential dead comparison (`cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` when externalCalendarId is already falsy) silently breaks per-host calendar targeting on update/delete. (P1, confidence 85)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent the fallback branch executes only when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` (and similarly for delete). Since `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null` in that branch, the `find` comparison is effectively dead and will return `undefined` unless a calendar has an undefined externalId. That means `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becomes undefined, defeating the intended fallback to a destination calendar and potentially causing updates/deletes to hit the wrong calendar (e.g., default/primary) or fail. This is a concrete logic bug introduced by the diff’s new array-based destinationCalendar handling.
